question: Does the physical tensor have a consistent directional response when inverse-Jacobian critical-curve amplification is removed?
interpretation: conditioning audit and unweighted source-plane closure diagnostic on spent systems; not an exact image prediction

geometry.source: P0562 two frozen zero-field optimizer ensembles
geometry.source_position_rule: unweighted arithmetic mean of training-image ray-shooting positions within each family
geometry.heldout_rule: Euclidean source-plane separation of the held-out image from its training-family mean
geometry.reason: never invert the image-to-source Jacobian, so a critical curve cannot manufacture an arbitrarily large response

claim_limits: Source-plane closure is conditioning-robust but is not the final image-plane likelihood.
The unweighted source estimator is a directional diagnostic, not an error-covariance model.
The geometry ensembles, systems, and coupling range are spent and provide no independent validation.
A common response would require confirmation with a stable exact global lens inference.
No formula can be promoted from P0563.
